metadata.summary: As England impressively levelled their three-match ODI series against Australia with a 135-run win in Adelaide, might they have stumbled upon the perfect bowling formula with one eye on the 2027 Cricket World Cup?
metadata.content: England beat Australia in second ODI: Sonny Baker new-ball switch from Jofra Archer pays off in Adelaide | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis England beat Australia in second ODI: Sonny Baker new-ball switch from Jofra Archer pays off in Adelaide Gus Atkinson (4-28) and Sonny Baker (1-45) reduce Australia to 29-4 in devastating opening spell as England bounce back from Perth drubbing to level ODI series with 135-run win in Adelaide; series decider takes place in Hobart on Wednesday (play starts at 3.30am, UK time) Sunday 15 November 2026 14:17, UK Image: Sonny Baker took 1-45 in eight overs after being given the new ball by England in the second ODI win over Australia As England impressively levelled their three-match ODI series against Australia with a 135-run win in Adelaide, might they have stumbled upon the perfect bowling formula with one eye on the 2027 Cricket World Cup? Tom Banton (121 off 99 balls) was rightly named Player of the Match for his second ODI hundred that helped turn things round after a dismal defeat in Perth - from 131 all out to 355-6 in the space of 48 hours - but the bowling was equally impressive. Image: England's Tom Banton celebrates his second ODI century against Australia in Adelaide Gus Atkinson (4-28) claimed career-best ODI figures as he and Sonny Baker (1-45) helped set the tone early on by reducing Australia to 29-4 in the opening seven overs of their run-chase as they were ultimately bowled out for 220. messages.text: Australia brush off New Zealand to win fourth straight Rugby League World Cup

metadata.summary: Jack Bostock and Liam Martin both starred as Australia swept away New Zealand 32-12 in the men's Rugby League World Cup final to be crowned world champions for the fourth time in a row.
metadata.content: Men's Rugby League World Cup final - Australia 32-12 New Zealand: Kangaroos brush off Kiwis to win fourth straight world title | Rugby League News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Men's Rugby League World Cup final - Australia 32-12 New Zealand: Kangaroos brush off Kiwis to win fourth straight world title Australia reigned supreme as they successfully defended their world title for the fourth consecutive time, as they beat New Zealand 32-12 in the men's Rugby League World Cup final Sunday 15 November 2026 11:55, UK Image: Australia won their fourth-straight Rugby League World Cup after defeating New Zealand on Sunday Jack Bostock and Liam Martin both starred as Australia swept away New Zealand 32-12 in the men's Rugby League World Cup final to be crowned world champions for the fourth time in a row. Australia had begun the tournament slowly, narrowly beating New Zealand 24-22 in their World Cup curtain-raiser in October, but when it came to the business end of the World Cup, they showcased why they are the best team in the world. It ushered in another era of dominance for Australian Rugby League, after the Jillaroos also completed a four-peat of World Cup victories, following their 34-10 victory against New Zealand's women's side earlier on Sunday. New Zealand had been out to win their first World Cup since 2008, but James Fisher-Harris' side were errant in defence, missing 37 tackles as Reece Walsh and Bradman Best tore apart the Kiwi line. messages.text: Rehan sends message to England with ton and five-for in Lions win

metadata.summary: Rehan Ahmed served the England selectors a reminder of his all-round talents by hitting a hundred and taking five-for in the Lions' fourth unofficial ODI win over West Indies A.
metadata.content: England Lions: Rehan Ahmed hits hundred and takes five-for in 80-run win over West Indies A | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content England Lions: Rehan Ahmed hits hundred and takes five-for in 80-run win over West Indies A Rehan Ahmed (108 off 100 balls) struck 11 fours and five sixes at No 3, before claiming 5-60 with his leg spin in the 80-run win; the Lions have won all seven of their matches on tour so far, following a 3-0 sweep in the T20 series by leading 4-0 in the five-match ODI leg Sunday 15 November 2026 09:10, UK Image: Rehan Ahmed reminded the England selectors of his talents with a terrific all-round display for the Lions in the West Indies Rehan Ahmed served the England selectors a reminder of his all-round talents by hitting a hundred and taking five-for in the Lions' fourth unofficial ODI win over West Indies A. Rehan (108 off 100 balls) struck 11 fours and five sixes at No 3 as the Lions - who had already clinched the series, leading 3-0 - posted 330 after winning the toss in St Kitts. The all-rounder then claimed 5-60 with his leg spin as the tourists bowled their opponents out for 250 overs in reply. The 22-year-old has played five Test matches, 11 ODIs and 14 T20s for England since making his debut as an 18-year-old in 2022.
